source_name: CKB careers portal (Talentlyft ATS)
why_relevant: CKB runs its vacancies through a hosted Talentlyft careers portal rather than plain HTML pages. Job titles here are the densest weak signal for team build-outs (cards, digital, compliance, AML) at the country's largest bank, and ATS pages usually expose structured listings that are easy to poll.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica — Karijera
why_relevant: NLB Podgorica posts named vacancies with closing dates in Montenegrin, historically in batches of ~10 covering exactly the weak-signal functions of interest: 'Direktor Odjeljenja platnog prometa i fintech-a', AML/'ovlašćeno lice za sprječavanje pranja novca', CRM i razvoj proizvoda, Data management. A short-link vacancy list at go.nlb.me/radna-mjesta was referenced as the live listing endpoint.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: The bank itself publishes 'ZAPOŠLJAVAMO: Trenutno otvorene radne pozicije' posts and staff-profile posts in Montenegrin on LinkedIn, often earlier and more granularly than on the website. It is the corporate channel that survives when a vacancy is pulled from the site.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — Organi upravljanja (Odbor direktora / Nadzorni odbor / Više rukovodstvo)
why_relevant: One of the most complete governance disclosures among ME banks: separate pages for Akcionari, Nadzorni odbor, Upravni odbor, Revizorski odbor, Više rukovodstvo, Ključne funkcije and an Organizaciona šema. The org chart page is a rare direct source for organisation changes, not just people changes; board membership (Montinari, Todorović, Njavro, Moniaci) is named.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — Obavještenja (news/notices)
why_relevant: The bank's own notice stream, where appointments, reorganisations and operational changes are announced in Montenegrin before they reach media. Note the term here is 'Obavještenja', not 'Vijesti' — a glossary variant that matters for query building. Mirror domain hb.co.me also observed serving the same site.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — Karijera / Aktuelni konkursi za zapošljavanje
why_relevant: Erste ME (~400 staff, >100k clients, >EUR 900m assets) maintains a dedicated 'Aktuelni konkursi za zapošljavanje' page plus a general karijera page with a CV inbox (cv@erstebank.me). The konkurs page is the direct hiring feed; the profile page carries scale figures useful for normalising headcount signals.

source_name: Addiko Bank AD Podgorica — Organi upravljanja
why_relevant: Addiko publishes its three-member Upravni odbor and governance structure in Montenegrin on its own site; Addiko has historically fronted named executives publicly (e.g. an izvršni direktor za komercijalne poslove appearing in media), so this page is the authoritative anchor for verifying who currently holds which executive portfolio.

source_name: Addiko Bank AD Podgorica — Zapošljavanje + Talentlyft portal
why_relevant: Addiko splits hiring across an on-site 'Zapošljavanje' section (including a 'Pošaljite CV' page) and a hosted Talentlyft board — the same ATS vendor CKB uses, meaning one parser covers two banks. Addiko ME is a consumer/SME lender, so its openings track cards and digital build-outs closely.

source_name: Addiko Bank AD Podgorica — Saopštenja za medije
why_relevant: Own press-release archive in Montenegrin covering strategic partnerships, product/digital launches and governance/transparency initiatives — the context layer that explains why a given hiring wave or reorganisation is happening.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — Karijera
why_relevant: Domestically owned bank with a simple, stable .php career page — easy to diff and unlikely to be JS-rendered. Prva banka is politically salient in Montenegro, so leadership changes there carry disproportionate signal value.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — Saopštenja
why_relevant: The bank's own Montenegrin-language announcements page — the channel where an appointment or shareholder/board decision at Prva banka would first appear in the bank's own words.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica — corporate site (karijera / o nama)
why_relevant: Fast-growing domestic bank (7th by assets in 2025, assets +11.65%, 51–200 staff) — exactly the profile that hires in bursts. Growth of this speed at this size makes its career and management pages a high-yield weak-signal source, though the exact karijera path was not confirmed in search results.

source_name: Universal Capital Bank AD Podgorica — About the Bank
why_relevant: Domestic bank (est. 2007, ~5% market share) whose corporate 'About the Bank' tree is the anchor for its governance and staffing narrative. Notable structural quirk: search surfaced two parallel path shapes (/en/about-the-bank/... and /en/about-us/...), suggesting a recent site migration — collection must handle both.

source_name: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica — Karijera
why_relevant: Adriatic Bank (ex-Nova Banka, rebranded under new ownership in March 2020, ~4.7% share) has a Montenegrin-language /me/karijera page and routes applications to hr@adriaticbank.com. A post-acquisition bank rebuilding its team is a prime hiring-signal target.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica — Karijera (sr)
why_relevant: Smallest licensed bank (11th, ~1.34% share, EUR 106m assets) but Turkish-parent-owned, and its career page explicitly pitches 'international banking knowledge'. Low absolute volume makes each posting individually informative; the /sr/ path confirms native-language coverage.

source_name: Zapad banka AD Podgorica — Rukovodstvo
why_relevant: A dedicated Montenegrin-language 'Rukovodstvo' page naming the bank's leaders — the cleanest single-URL leadership source in the cell. Zapad banka jumped to 5th by assets in 2025 with +19.16% growth, the fastest in the system, so leadership and hiring there are high-priority weak signals.

source_name: CBCG — Banke u Crnoj Gori (useful links / bank website directory)
why_relevant: Regulator-maintained directory of the banks' own website addresses — the cheapest authoritative way to resolve each licensed bank to its current corporate domain, which is precisely the seed list this coverage cell needs and the thing most likely to go stale after a rebrand (e.g. Nova Banka to Adriatic Bank).

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — banking association
why_relevant: All 11 licensed banks are members; its Skupština sessions elect an Upravni odbor whose chair is typically a sitting bank CEO (Erste's Aleksa Lukić held that post), making association news a leading indicator of who is currently the top executive at a member bank. It also published a new Statut and a 2026–2031 framework, and issues the 'Bankar' journal archive as PDFs.

source_name: bankar.me — Montenegrin banking trade portal
why_relevant: Republishes and amplifies banks' own hiring and appointment announcements in Montenegrin, often with the vacancy list quoted in full ('NLB banka zapošljava na deset pozicija') and executive-election stories ('Izvršni direktor Erste banke Aleksa Lukić izabran za predsjednika Upravnog Odbora Udruženja banaka'). Critically, it preserves postings after banks delete them — a durable archive for expired vacancies.

source_name: Portal Analitika / RTCG — Montenegrin general media banking coverage
why_relevant: Mainstream Montenegrin outlets carry the 'novi glavni izvršni direktor' stories with career-history detail that bank governance pages omit (prior employers, start dates, internal promotion path). Useful as the corroboration layer that dates a leadership move when the bank's own page shows only a current-state roster with no timestamp.

source_name: thebanks.eu — Montenegro bank profiles (size/rank baseline)
why_relevant: Provides comparable asset, market-share and rank figures per Montenegrin bank (e.g. Zapad 5th/+19.16%, Lovćen 7th/+11.65%, Ziraat 11th/1.34%). Not a hiring source, but it is the normaliser that turns raw vacancy counts from the corporate channels into growth-adjusted signal and tells the analyst which small bank's three openings actually matter.

source_name: Montenegro Securities Commission (SCMN) — issuer pages for listed banks
why_relevant: Banks are joint-stock companies (AD) and appear as emitenti (issuers) on the securities-commission site. Issuer filings are where board elections and statutory changes are legally disclosed, giving a dated, authoritative corroboration for governance changes that a bank's own 'Menadžment' page shows only as a silent edit.

source_name: Payten Montenegro (Asseco Group) - corporate news & Montenegro country page
why_relevant: Payten is described in Montenegrin-market material as the leading ATM/POS provider in Montenegro, present since 2006, with long-term relationships with 9 of ~11 banks, 28 staff locally. Its news feed publishes bank-by-bank implementation announcements (e.g. SoftPOS at Hipotekarna banka), which simultaneously reveal a Montenegrin bank project and Payten's own local organisational build-out.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC) - member profile pages (Payten and other vendors)
why_relevant: MFIC member profiles carry unusually concrete Montenegro-specific vendor facts: local headcount, number of ATMs/POS deployed, number of bank customers, year of market entry. It is also an actor map for which international suppliers actually have a registered Montenegrin presence, and members' representatives are named, which surfaces country-manager-level people.

source_name: Printec Montenegro - country page (Printec Group)
why_relevant: Printec Montenegro (present since 2014) publishes its local footprint: ~15+ staff, service centres in Podgorica, Ulcinj, Budva, Herceg Novi, and team functions (Business Development, Sales, Customer Support, Professional Services). Changes to this page are a direct signal of local office openings, headcount growth and function build-out in the transaction-automation supplier layer serving ME banks.

source_name: Logate (Podgorica) - customer/reference and CX360 banking product pages
why_relevant: Domestic Podgorica software vendor that publicly names its Montenegrin bank customers for its banking CRM (Erste Montenegro, NLB Podgorica, CKB/OTP, Hipotekarna, Lovcen banka, Prva banka, AIK). Reference-page changes reveal new bank projects; the About/careers pages reveal headcount and hiring in the bank-facing delivery teams.

source_name: Logate LinkedIn company page (me.linkedin.com)
why_relevant: Vendor LinkedIn pages are the fastest-moving indicator of hires, new roles and leadership announcements in the Montenegrin bank-supplier layer; the .me subdomain confirms Montenegro registration.
